_provenance.source_title: Vision Zero DC coalition & pitch-target inventory
_provenance.source_description: Named recipients who can act on this project's findings, the channel they act through, and the DC calendar moment to reach them. Government bodies, pro-safety advocacy coalitions, and the opposition landscape to anticipate.
_provenance.methodology: Web-verified 2026-07-09 during PLAN.md Workstream D2. Every entry links its primary source URL. Officeholders, roles, and meeting cadences were confirmed as of that date; re-check names and URLs before pitching. This is a pitch-routing tool, not an endorsement or an exhaustive directory.
caveats: Officeholders and committee assignments change; re-verify the chair and committee scope each Council period.
Meeting cadences are the published recurring schedule; individual meetings get cancelled or moved — check the body's own calendar before showing up.
'can_act_on' maps a target to this project's finding types; it does not claim the target has taken a position on any specific finding.
The opposition landscape is included so pitches anticipate documented counter-arguments with data, not to disparage residents raising real concerns (congestion, ADA access, business impact).

targets.name: DC Council Committee on Transportation & the Environment
targets.role: Primary legislative venue. Chaired by Charles Allen in Council Period 26; oversees DDOT among 26 agencies. Performance oversight hearings ran Jan–Feb 2026; budget oversight ~Mar–May.

targets.name: DDOT Vision Zero Office + Highway Safety Office (HSO)
targets.role: HSO sits within DDOT's Project Delivery Administration – Vision Zero, is NHTSA-grant-funded, runs the 'United We Go' campaign, and hosts the 2026 Mobility Safety Summit — a direct demo venue for this tool.

targets.name: Bicycle Advisory Council (BAC)
targets.role: Official public body advising the Mayor and Council. Members testify at oversight hearings.

targets.name: Pedestrian Advisory Council (PAC)
targets.role: Official public body advising the Mayor and Council on pedestrian safety. Named partner on the insurance-modernization push.

targets.name: Major Crash Review Task Force
targets.role: Independent public body reviewing all fatal crashes; includes MPD, DDOT, OP, DMV, BAC, PAC, MAAC. Directly relevant to the memo-delivery audit.

targets.name: ANC Vision Zero Caucus + ward Councilmembers
targets.role: The ANC Vision Zero Caucus was revived in fall 2025 (WABA organizing) — a purpose-built audience for the ANC brief page. Each ward's Councilmember and ANCs are reachable via the site's resolution generator.

targets.name: DC Families for Safe Streets
targets.role: Flagship alignment. Three current campaigns map 1:1 onto this project: B26-0057 insurance modernization, Intelligent Speed Assistance, and 'Fund & Implement Safe Streets Legislation' (their listed laws are almost exactly data/legislation.json). Our law tracker + delivery-audit pointers are ready-made evidence infrastructure for their existing campaign — lead the first pitch here.

targets.name: Washington Area Bicyclist Association (WABA)
targets.role: Testifies every oversight/budget season; publishes an annual 'DDOT oversight take' each January; hosts the Washington Region Vision Zero Summit; organized the ANC VZ Caucus revival. The enforcement-mismatch and warnings findings are testimony-grade.

targets.name: Insurance-reform coalition around B26-0057
targets.role: Pre-assembled audience per WABA advocacy pages: WABA, DC Families for Safe Streets, DC PAC, MADD, DC Multimodal Accessibility Council, Institute for Safer Trucking, Truck Safety Coalition, BAC. A ready audience for any crash-severity / KSI findings.

targets.name: Amplification network
targets.role: Reach beyond the core coalition: Greater Greater Washington, Coalition for Smarter Growth, DC Transportation Equity Network, Bike Walk & Bus PAC, Washington Parks and People.

targets.name: DC Safe Streets Coalition (bike-lane opposition — name collision)
targets.role: NOT a pro-safety group despite the name. Neighbors organizing against DDOT protected-bike-lane projects (17th St NW, Kansas Ave, Missouri Ave, Taylor St) and for e-bike regulation. Two implications: (a) name collision — always link the exact org URL; (b) their stated concerns (congestion, ADA compliance, business access) are the counter-arguments pitch kits should anticipate with data, not dismiss.

calendar_hooks.note: A direct pitch/demo venue for this tool.

first_pitch_sequence.why: Offer the law tracker + delivery-audit as evidence infrastructure for their 'Fund & Implement' campaign — 1:1 overlap with data/legislation.json. Needs no new A-finding to start.
Time it to oversight-season prep (their annual DDOT-oversight post lands in January); enforcement-mismatch and warnings findings are testimony-grade.
The ANC brief page is purpose-built for this audience.
HSO Mobility Safety Summit / WABA regional VZ Summit are demo venues for the tool itself.
